Pet Ransom

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It's bad enough losing your pet, but what do you do when someone is holding it for ransom?

Unique Selling Point:
Interview with Cape Town case study who paid R1500 to get her cat back, only to find she'd been scammed. The ransom was drawn from an ATM in KZN, but even though she opened a case at SAPS, they failed to investigate.
WhatsApp voice notes from aggressive seamster called Jason.

Lynne Earley posted a fake lost dog notice and within an hour was contacted by "Paul Govender" claiming to know where the dog is. The ransom went from R700 to R300 in a series of WhatsApp voice notes which we have.


Summary:
Cats, dogs and birds go missing every day and distraught owners usually post a photo with information on one of the many Lost & Found Pets pages on Facebook. A syndicate has emerged that calls the owners claiming to be in the same neighbourhood and that his 'maid' knows where the pet is. He then demands R1000 to share the information. As negotiations proceed the amount decreases, from R500 to R400 to R300 deposit, to just R50 for airtime. When you ask for proof of life, the 'petnapper' claims his 'maid's' phone doesn't have a phone, or his WhatsApp isn't working.
Sometimes the caller is aggressive, sometimes sort of reasonable. The numbers come up as 'SAPS', or 'SAPS Organised Crime' on TrueCaller. Some numbers have also shown pnaidoo@saps.gov.za. One scammer claims his name is Paul Govender. One number has been traced to B Naidoo in Tongaat, KZN.
This scam has been reported all over the country in several provinces. It seems that there are only a handful of seamsters doing it.

Further information:
One couple whose golden retriever Fiela went missing in Durbanville, Cape Town put up fliers and many notices on Facebook. They were contacted by an Uber driver who claimed to have the dog, but when pushed for information disappeared.
Then they were inundated with messages from people recommending pet communicators. They claimed they had managed to trace their lost pets with their help. Out of desperation Renate Coetzee paid a pet communicator R500, but was fed unhelpful nonsense over WhatsApp.

Flights to Cape Town, car rental, accommodation

Script:


PET RANSOM

V/O: “Our perfect companions never have fewer than four feet” wrote French author Colette. As part of the family, dogs and cats have a special place in our hearts and homes. And any pet-owner knows the rollercoaster that follows if they ever go missing.

Link: The panic, the frantic search, the anxiety as you imagine the worst. And then the massive relief when you get a message that your beloved animal has been found. Or has it?

Fransje: I adopted George from foster care three years ago, and he’s an absolutely lovely cat. And we live in the greenbelt here. So he used to go down to the greenbelt, come back up again, but he would always be around. And then one day he went off after breakfast and that was it.

V/O: Fransje van Riel lives in Cape Town. After her cat George went missing she put up posters in the area and on several Facebook groups. Two weeks later she got a WhatsApp message.

Fransje: It just said ‘Hi, I’m also in Constantia. I know where your cat is. And my maid, who also works in Constantia, has your cat and she’s going to give him to her daughter who lives out of town.’ I had heard of pet scamming already so my red flags were going up immediately.

V/O But, Candice Johnstone and Anton Munnik had never heard of pet scamming when their cat Hazel went missing from their complex in Brackenfell.

Candice: We posted a reward for R1000 on the advert on Facebook and then also on the printed flyer.

Anton: About a week later someone called me and said that they have Hazel. They were saying that they were driving in the main road across here and that they had to swerve away. Then they said they ran after Hazel, caught Hazel, and now they have Hazel and a damaged tyre and they want us to pay for the repairs.

Bongani: What were they asking you for?

Anton: They were asking at that time for R5000.

Link: Pet napping – real or fake – how would you know what to do? Well who better to ask than a hostage negotiator.

Herman: First of all I would want to see a video clip of the pet where I can identify that is my pet.

V/O: Herman Bosman was the provincial commander of the police’s Hostage Negotiation Team for 20 years.

Herman: Proof of life or proof of having what you claim you have is very, very important. If they cannot prove that they have what they claim they do, then obviously there’s no negotiations from that point onwards.

Candice: We sent him R200 airtime because he claimed that he didn’t have airtime to send us a picture and he said he will send it tonight.

V/O: Proof of life never arrived, but the scammer - who calls himself Jason - continued to play cat and mouse.

Anton: He was saying I know I have your cat. She has a pink paw pad on the left side.

Bongani: Why was the pink paw enough for you to hand over money?

Anton: She’s a completely black cat, and her having one pink paw pad on her left paw is not very…

Candice: It’s not common.

V/O: Having hooked them with the southpaw, Jason conned Candice into believing she would soon be reunited with Hazel.

Voice Note:
Jason: You go to Spar, you tell them you want to send R1500 to this number.

Candice: We first need to see a picture of the cat then we will send it.

Jason: You’re not hearing what I’m telling you. You’re not hearing me. I’m 2 minutes away from you, I’m in the area.

Candice: You will bring her to me?

Jason: You give me the receipt, you give me the balance of the cash, and you take your cat and I take my cash and I go pay my car off.

Candice: Ok I will go and do that right now. I live very close to the Spar.

Candice: Then I got a slip with an OTP or PIN or something like that and I had to send that to Jason.

Bongani: And at this stage you still have no proof?

Candice: No proof, no proof. But he was so aggressive, so aggressive. And then eventually I sent him the PIN and obviously he then disappeared. But then we knew, yeah he never had her, it was all a lie.

V/O: The money was withdrawn from Standard Bank in Pietermaritzburg. The scam is running nation-wide: from Cape Town to Witbank, Pretoria to Bloemfontein. In almost every province, we found cases of scammers claiming to know the whereabouts of missing pets, when they really don’t have a clue. What they do know is how to manipulate you. And every day, victims are paying up.

Laura: He wanted R300 upfront, then the balance after he’d given me the address.

V/O: When Laura Young’s cat Wobbles went missing in Alberton, she was contacted by a Paul Naidoo who claimed to be in the area. She agreed to pay to get her cat back.

Laura: He then gave me an account number, and I said I need a name. He gave me the name R. Mangroo. So I then did the R300 transfer. I sent him proof of payment, and he said no, his maid now wants R500 to show trust.

V/O: Wobbles is still missing and Laura R500 poorer. The matter is being investigated by her bank and the police.

Link: It’s easy to think how could they fall for it? How could they just roll over and pay the “ransom”? But bereft and desperate, pet owners’ emotions make them sitting ducks for scamsters.

Lynne: That’s my biggest fear to lose my dog or dogs. And I think you’ll do anything. You’ll believe anything.

V/O: Lynne Earley is a bit of an amateur pet detective – who tried to help Candice and Anton.

Lynne: I wrote a letter to the Brigadier in Natal and I said Candice had this situation of being scammed. And he replied and just said we have to apply for a 205 and sort of like it’s too much work. And then also people shouldn’t be so naïve. So that was the feedback I got from SAPS.

V/O: So she decided to bait the pet scammer herself by putting a fake post on Facebook, using a fake picture of a dog.

Bongani: What did your post say?

Lynne: I just said I’ve lost my dog in Sea Point. I’m looking for him all over, you know. Could you please phone me?

V/O: Within hours she received this voice note which followed the usual script:

Paul: Hi yes, it’s my maid who works for me, she works for another white lady as well. This white lady also has your dog. She knows it’s yours, she doesn’t want to give it back – actually her daughter is coming to take it in the next hour or so. And I can give you all the details, you can drive past, get it. But keep it discreet and anonymous.

V/O: Then came the demand for money - for a dog that doesn’t exist.

Paul: My maid also found out you have a reward for this dog, so my maid wants to charge you an amount of R1000. You pay R400 first, you get the address, you get the dog, then you pay the R600 balance. Or you pay 300 first, it’s up to you, the ball is in your court. If you don’t want to do it, it’s fine. I’m an Indian guy, I’m not here to bulls***t you.

Bongani: Did he say who he was?

Lynne: His name was a Paul Govender. His cell number has got a SAPS email address. His True Caller ID is a SAPS Organised Crime.

V/O: It’s unclear whether being Indian or being a policeman is meant to inspire confidence, but this scammer poses as Detective Warrant Officer Paul Govender from Bloemfontein. Carte Blanche can confirm the Police have never heard of him and the persona is fake. Lynne decided to send him R200 anyway just to track his whereabouts.

Lynne: I paid him R200, and within minutes, I think literally 3 minutes he withdrew it in Durban.

V/O: The R200 was withdrawn from an ABSA ATM in Durban’s China Mall.

Link: Is it Paul, is it Jason, is it Mr Naidoo, is it Mr Govender, or even Mangroo? I’ve got a whole list of numbers here.

V/O: We tried calling over 20 numbers that had been used by the scammers but couldn’t get through to any of them. They hadn’t been RICA’d which means they’re untraceable. But one number was registered to a Mrs Naidoo at an address in Tongaat Beach. We decided to pay her a visit.

Nicky: We’re looking for a man called Paul Naidoo.

Naidoo: Paul?

Nicky: Paul. Not you?

Naidoo: No. My name’s Bhala Naidoo.

Nicky: Mrs Yaganayagi Naidoo, who’s that?

Naidoo: Well that was my wife.

Nicky: Was your wife – she passed?

Nicky: Ja.

Nicky: I’m so sorry uncle.

Naidoo: Ten years ago.

Nicky: Ten years ago.

Herman: Scamming is nothing new. And I think pet scamming is just a new way where they work on somebody’s emotions and love for the animals and pets.

Bongani: How would you categorize this crime? Is it extortion?

Herman: It’s definitely extortion. It can definitely amount to obtaining an advantage from somebody else. Playing on your emotions.

V/O: Ironically Hazel the cat was found safe and sound and returned home two months later.

Link: In our investigation of over 20 cases only 3 people actually reported the scam to the police. Some saw right through it; others were simply too embarrassed to approach the authorities. But even if they had, would there have been an investigation?

Herman: I think that the problem in most of the cases is the money paid and the money involved doesn’t justify spending a lot of money on investigation and trying to retrieve the perpetrator.I think there may be many more people. Get a group together, and if there’s a definite syndicate in this, I think the police will then have to look into this.

The numbers come up as 'SAPS', or 'SAPS Organised Crime' on TrueCaller. Some numbers have also shown pnaidoo@saps.gov.za. One scammer claims his name is Paul Govender. One number has been traced to B Naidoo in Tongaat, KZN. This scam has been reported all over the country in several provinces. It seems that there are only a handful of seamsters doing it.
metadata.Further information: One couple whose golden retriever Fiela went missing in Durbanville, Cape Town put up fliers and many notices on Facebook. They were contacted by an Uber driver who claimed to have the dog, but when pushed for information disappeared. Then they were inundated with messages from people recommending pet communicators. They claimed they had managed to trace their lost pets with their help. Out of desperation Renate Coetzee paid a pet communicator R500, but was fed unhelpful nonsense over WhatsApp.
